Under Clause 13.3.1, a shuttle is out only if it lands outside the boundaries of the court (i.e. not on or within the boundary lines), meaning landing on a line is not a fault. Additionally, according to Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5) (in force 2025-04-26), Clause 8.4, if the shuttle lands in, the Line Judge shall say nothing, but point to the line with the right hand while looking towards the Umpire.

question: How do we check whether a shuttle has the right speed?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: 'The sources do not say how we check whether a shuttle has the right speed.' The Laws answer it directly: Law 3.1 (1)–(2) gives the test stroke (full underhand stroke contacting the shuttle over the back boundary line, hit at an upward angle parallel to the side lines), and Law 3.2 (1) gives the pass criterion (a shuttle of correct speed lands not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line, per Diagram B). ITTO 3.5.4.1 (1) adds who performs the test (an active player, preferably male, or a qualified person approved by the Referee), which is part of how the check is done. Related but not answering the 'how': ITTO 3.5.4.4 (1) on assessing the result (manner of hit, correct location) and ITTO 3.6.3 (1) on the Referee re-checking during play that the selected speed still appears correct.
answer.answer:
To check whether a shuttle has the right speed, the shuttle should be tested by an active player in the tournament, preferably a male player, or a qualified person approved by the Referee (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 3.5.4.1). The tester shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line, and the shuttle shall be hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 3.1). A shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 3.2).
Related (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), Clause 3.5.4.4): "When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit (strength of shot and trajectory), and whether they were hit from the correct location (over the back line) (Law 3)."
Related (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), Clause 3.6.3): "Shuttle Speed The Referee shall at all times, when observing play, consider whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct."
